content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-maths-multiplication-facts","title":"Multiplication Facts & Balancing","quick":"Both sides of the equal sign must give the same total. First find the answer on the known side, then find what number times the other factor gives that same answer.","full":"An equal sign means both sides are the same amount, like a balance scale at a kirana shop - if one pan has 100 rupees worth of goods, the other pan must also have 100 rupees worth. Here, 100 times 5 equals 500. So the right side, 25 times blank, must also equal 500. We ask: 25 times what gives 500? Count by 25s: 25,50,75...500 is the 20th jump, so the answer is 20. Check: 25 times 20 is 500, same as 100 times 5.","tip":"Think of a balance: both pans must weigh the same, so find the total first, then match it.","answer":"20","traps":["Multiplying 100×5 but writing 100 as the missing number instead of solving for it","Forgetting to find the total (500) first before dividing","Guessing a small number like 5 without checking 25×5 only gives 125"],"misconception":"Child thinks the blank should just copy a number already in the problem instead of calculating what makes both sides equal.","parent_questions":[{"q":"What is 100 times 5?","expected_answer_hint":"Should say 500 confidently."},{"q":"If 25 times blank equals 500, how do you find the blank?","expected_answer_hint":"Should say divide 500 by 25, or count 25s up to 500."}],"check_question":{"q":"50 × 4 = 20 × ____","options":["10","4","20"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Yes! 50×4=200, and 20×10=200.","wrong_feedback":"Try again: first find 50×4, then see what times 20 gives that same number."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A simple balance scale at a small Indian shop with equal piles of coins on both sides, a shopkeeper watching to make sure both sides balance.","labels":[{"text":"balance","position":"top"}]}}
